newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close at session highs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close at session highs.

text.p: Argentine stocks stretched gains at the close Monday, powered by a Wall Street rally, dealers said.

"Investors are shrugging off an expected small U.S. interest rate hike, which they believe wouldn't be traumatic for the markets or hurt the economic outlook of listed companies," said Dario Lizzano, head of research at Santander Investments.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 1.6 percent to 741.91, extending last week's 2.6 percent recovery after a losing spell earlier in March.

"The bolsa has clearly resumed its upward course and today it was aided by a technical rebound in the New York markets ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee decision on rates Tuesday," one trader said.
The broad market closed up 1.1 percent, with winners bashing losers 41 to five and 17 issues closing flat.

Floor volume slowed to 20.3 million pesos from 25.7 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover rose to 197.4 million pesos from 180.2 million. Traders said the hefty OTC volume reflected end-of-month position-squaring (markets are closed Thursday and Friday for the Easter holidays).
Top MerVal performers included steelmakers Acindar and Siderca, which shot up 5.0 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
"Acindar's prices have a lot of growth potential because it sells to the construction sector which is booming, and it is undergoing a restructuring process," said Lizzano.
He noted Siderca, while one of Argentina's leading exporters producing at full capacity, had also become a virtual holding company with subsidiaries in other countries undergoing promising reforms.
Other top MerVal risers were petrochemical concern Indupa and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, up 3.4 percent and 2.4 percent respectively.
The only blue-chip loser was carmaker Ciadea, off 0.3 percent, while real estate developer Irsa closed flat.
